anchor: GS3.1 Indian economy: monetary policy, liquidity management and financial stability
argumentsAgainst: The source does not provide the size or direction of the liquidity imbalance beyond RBI’s reference to current and evolving liquidity conditions.
A VRRR auction is a short-term liquidity operation and, by itself, does not establish a change in the monetary-policy stance.
argumentsFor: The auction provides RBI a mechanism to absorb liquidity temporarily through a market-based operation.
The specified reversal date makes the operation time-bound rather than a permanent withdrawal of liquidity.
background: RBI uses liquidity-management operations under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) to influence short-term liquidity conditions.

indiaImplications: The notified operation may help RBI manage short-term liquidity conditions in the banking system.
The two-day tenor and scheduled reversal indicate a temporary intervention; the source does not establish its effect on inflation, credit growth or market yields.
Banks and market participants must account for the auction window and reversal date in their short-term liquidity planning.

mainsPractice.stem: Explain how the RBI’s announced VRRR auction can function as a temporary liquidity-management instrument. What are the limits of inferring monetary-policy intent from this announcement?

officialFacts.text: The Reserve Bank of India decided to conduct a Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction on Tuesday, November 17, 2026.
The notified amount for the auction is ₹50,000 crore.
The auction window is 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM.
The date of reversal is November 19, 2026 (Thursday).
The operational guidelines for the auction as given in the Reserve Bank’s Press Release 2019-2020/1947 dated February 13, 2020 will remain the same.

example.heading: Illustration
example.text: Suppose a bank temporarily places funds with RBI through the announced auction. The funds would be unavailable to that bank during the two-day tenor and would be reversed on the scheduled date; this is only a hypothetical illustration of the time-bound design, not a reported transaction.

pocketRead.excerpt: RBI announced a ₹50,000-crore, two-day VRRR auction for November 17, with the funds scheduled for reversal on November 19.

question.answer: The announcement supports the inference that RBI is using a temporary, auction-based instrument to manage liquidity. It does not by itself prove the size of any liquidity surplus, a change in the policy rate or the eventual macroeconomic effect.
question.prompt: How should an aspirant interpret the RBI’s announced VRRR auction without overstating its monetary-policy significance?

sections.heading: What RBI announced
paragraphs: RBI announced a Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction for November 17, 2026, with a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore, a two-day tenor and a 09:30 AM–10:00 AM window. The funds are scheduled for reversal on November 19, 2026.

sections.heading: Mechanism and limitation
paragraphs: The time-bound design indicates an instrument for temporary liquidity management under the LAF. The source says the decision followed a review of current and evolving liquidity conditions, but it does not specify the underlying diagnosis or establish that the auction changes the monetary-policy stance.

recallCard: On November 17, 2026, RBI will conduct a ₹50,000-crore, two-day VRRR auction under LAF from 09:30–10:00 AM; reversal is scheduled for November 19. It is a temporary liquidity operation, not conclusive evidence of a policy-stance change.
sourceTitle: RBI to conduct 2-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction under LAF on November 17, 2026
staticDefinition: A Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction is an auction-based RBI operation in which liquidity is temporarily placed with the central bank at a variable rate; the supplied record identifies it under the LAF but does not itself provide the full operational definition.
use: Use the announcement to illustrate the distinction between short-term liquidity management and a durable change in monetary-policy stance.

advisory_notes: The background definition of VRRR is sound analytical context, but the supplied extract refers readers to the 2020 guidelines rather than reproducing them.
The claim that VRRR absorbs liquidity is a standard mechanism explanation; label it as mechanism rather than as a fact stated in this announcement.
The statement that temporary absorption can support orderly money-market conditions is plausible analysis, not an outcome established by the announcement.
The phrase “funds would be unavailable to that bank” in the illustration is broadly correct but should note that the hypothetical concerns successfully placed funds, not the entire notified amount.
The recall card’s phrase “RBI will conduct” is acceptable for the announced operation, but “funds are scheduled for reversal” should not imply that the auction had already occurred.
The proposed GS3.1 anchor is relevant to monetary policy and liquidity management; financial stability is a broader association than this release itself establishes.
The headline and pocketRead deck accurately capture the announcement, subject to the announcement’s future-tense status on November 16, 2026.

wayForward: Interpret the operation alongside subsequent liquidity, money-market and policy communications rather than in isolation.
Preserve the distinction between what RBI officially announced and what analysts infer about the underlying liquidity conditions.
Assess effectiveness through observable market and banking-system outcomes, which are not supplied in this record.
whyInNews: The Reserve Bank of India announced on November 16, 2026, that it would conduct a two-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility on November 17, 2026. The auction has a notified amount of ₹50,000 crore, a 09:30 AM–10:00 AM window and reversal scheduled for November 19, 2026.
